subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should first-time non-empty `agents.list` without `default: true` continue to make the first listed agent the default, or should OpenClaw warn, reject, or auto-preserve `main` when existing `main` state would be displaced?
rationale: All viable fixes intentionally change documented default-routing semantics or config-write UX, and the compatibility/security tradeoff needs maintainer intent before automation chooses an implementation.

options.title: Require or prompt for explicit default
options.body: Keep runtime parsing compatible, but make CLI/UI/doctor setup flows warn or fail before a first listed agent displaces existing implicit `main` state without `default: true`.

options.title: Warn only
options.body: Preserve first-entry fallback everywhere and add high-visibility warning plus docs/doctor guidance for users adding their first listed agent.

options.title: Auto-preserve main
options.body: Materialize `main` as the default when `main` state exists, protecting continuity but changing the meaning of first-entry-only configs.

recommendation.title: Require or prompt for explicit default
recommendation.body: Keep runtime parsing compatible, but make CLI/UI/doctor setup flows warn or fail before a first listed agent displaces existing implicit `main` state without `default: true`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the multi-agent routing/default behavior and is the strongest history signal for the policy decision.
